{"basis":"measured","confidence":1.0,"fact_type":"measurement","name":"MEASURED on real RocksDB with a RELEASE binary: the two calls documented as cheap orientation reads cost ~11.5s each, and ~10s of that is detect_defects riding along on a reply nobody asked it of","statement":"MEASURED 2026-08-21 through the REAL MCP tool surface, driven over stdio against a REAL RocksDB store built from reflow2's own committed export (2862 nodes, 12139 edges, 8 MB on disk). Both build profiles, because users run release binaries and developers run debug.

                      debug      RELEASE
  get_node            0.01s       0.00s
  scan_nodes          0.11s       0.01s
  export_graph        3.10s       0.36s
  detect_gaps         3.11s       0.51s
  detect_defects     40.8s       10.3s     <== the hot spot
  loop_status        47.5s       11.4s
  open_questions     50.6s       11.7s     <== the FIRST call of every session
  graph_report    45–92s       10.9–22.4s

⭐ THE FINDING: `detect_defects` COSTS ~10s AND RIDES ALONG ON CALLS THAT NEVER ASKED FOR IT. `loop_status` reports a structural-defect count so it pays; `open_questions` pays it through the `loop_hint` attached to its reply. `open_questions` does its own work in about half a second and costs 11.7. So the two calls this project's own instructions call the cheap orientation reads — the SessionStart hook, the server instructions and the Stop hook all push an agent at them — are the two most expensive calls on the surface, and neither is expensive because of what it was asked to do.

🛑 AND IT CORRECTS A STANDING BELIEF. "The first store read of a session costs 26–48s" has been carried as a known cost and read as the STORE being slow. It is not the store: `get_node` is sub-millisecond and `scan_nodes` is 10ms on the real backend. The cost is a whole-design sweep bolted onto an orientation reply.

=== TWO HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED FIRST, both cheap, both recorded so nobody re-runs them ===

(1) THAT THE SYNC CHECK WAS READING AND HASHING EVERY KNOWN EXPORT FILE. `sync_debt` does exactly that per path in `last_synced` — read, full serde_json parse, SHA-256, verify — and this design has ~15 such paths, several at 7.5 MB. FALSIFIED: a probe store with `last_synced` EMPTY still took 46.5s.
(2) THAT `export_graph` INSIDE THE DEBT COMPUTATION WAS THE COST. FALSIFIED: 3.1s debug, 0.36s release.

The cause was found by timing each tool in an ISOLATED fresh process, which also ruled out ordering and cache effects — `detect_gaps` measured 3.11 / 3.06 / 3.11 while `open_questions` measured 50.59 / 50.44 / 50.86.

=== WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED ===

WHY `detect_defects` costs 20x what `detect_gaps` costs over the same graph. Both sweep the whole design; nothing here looks inside either. That ratio is the next measurement and it has not been taken.

NOTHING WAS OPTIMISED. Anthony's call — "we can optimize another day". The likely fix is to REMOVE the work rather than speed it up: do not compute a defect sweep for a reply nobody asked it of, which would take `open_questions` from ~11.7s to ~0.6s on the call every session makes first. Recorded as a target, not a plan; the optimize skill wants a derived budget written before any change and none has been.

⚠️ BOUND: one machine, one design, one shape of design. The RATIOS are the transferable part; the absolute seconds are not.","subject_id":"cmp:service","valid_from":"2026-08-21","valid_to":""}
